# Budgets and the two optimization methods

This guide covers the numeric engines selected by explicit `optimization` and
`penalty` arguments. Use `?CECoptimizers` for the full list of control fields.
No algorithm or penalty is changed by the display helpers.

## One execution versus repeated diagnostics

For an EM-bank grid, one execution fits each soft order from 1 to `Rmax`
with `Ninit` starts. It ranks its resulting hard partitions over all cells.
Increasing the number of grid cells does not repeat these EM fits, although
hard scoring, diagnostics and result construction still cost time and memory.

`k0=L` executions on the original sample and `B` executions on independent
bootstrap samples produce the diagnostics. Increasing `Ninit` improves each
execution's search budget; increasing L or B changes the diagnostic replication.
These controls cannot be substituted for one another.

The CEM route runs searches at each grid cell. Its `Rmax` is an initial search
order, not a strict final cap; `rinit_max` and `max_batches` bound later search.
`min_child` controls subdivision starts, not minimum final cluster size.
`saturation_stop` can stop the search and is separate from the diagram's
`sat_threshold`. These distinctions matter when reproducing a budget.

## A paired four-way example

```{r data}
set.seed(26)
X <- cbind(c(rnorm(20,-2,0.6),rnorm(20,2,0.6)),rnorm(40,sd=0.6))
```

We use small CEM batches and a small EM bank below. This tests the interface;
the budgets do not establish comparable optimization quality.

```{r four-way}
fits <- list()
for (method in c("cem","em_bank")) {
  for (penalty in c("none","bic")) {
    key <- paste(method,penalty,sep="_")
    fits[[key]] <- CECclassif(X,C=1,lambda=1,
      optimization=method,penalty=penalty,
      optimizer_control=list(Rmax=3,Ninit=1,max_iter=20,
        max_batches=1,seed=6))
  }
}
data.frame(method=names(fits),
  groups=vapply(fits,function(f)f$REO,0),
  objective=vapply(fits,function(f)f$objective,0))
```

Compare objective values only at the same data, C, lambda and penalty. BIC
values and unpenalized values are different criteria. EM log likelihood and
the hard objective are also different quantities. The stored `Hphi` is the
objective divided by lambda; it is not the unnormalized `H_lambda` field.

## Inspect convergence and failed starts

```{r convergence}
em <- fits$em_bank_none
data.frame(order=vapply(em$bank$starts,function(s)s$r,0),
  valid=vapply(em$bank$starts,function(s)s$valid,TRUE),
  reason=vapply(em$bank$starts,function(s)s$stop,""))
fits$cem_bic$solver$status
```

The EM bank stores attempted starts, validity, stop reasons and likelihood
traces, including failed starts that did not enter the bank. Duplicate
candidates do not remove the record of their generating starts. A hard trivial
baseline remains available even when a regular EM fit fails on singular data.
Finding only that candidate is a reason to inspect the records and data,
not evidence that the numerical search exhaustively established one group.

Numeric CEM stores search and descent records. Accepted moves decrease the
refitted hard objective, including the chosen penalty. Budget stops are
distinguished from lack of further accepted moves. A stop reason is not a
global optimality certificate.

## Cmax, target C and candidate reuse

```{r base-grid}
g <- CECfitBoundGrid(Z=X,C_grid=c(0.25,1),lambda_grid=c(0.6,1,1.5),
  optimization="em_bank",penalty="none",k0=3,B=3,algo_seed=17,
  optimizer_control=list(Rmax=3,Ninit=1,Cmax=2,max_iter=30),
  rsi_policy="all",n_cores=1)
fine <- CECrescoreGrid(g,C_grid=c(0.25,0.5,1,2),
  lambda_grid=seq(0.6,1.5,length.out=7),penalty="bic")
nrow(fine$summary)
```

The original soft fits obey `Cmax=2`. The later hard profiles are recomputed
under each target C, which may be smaller. Rescoring at C greater than Cmax
is rejected. A larger Cmax must be chosen before fitting a bank that will be
used for such targets. Reusing a finite bank does not make its search exhaustive
over all hard partitions.

Changing the penalty does not require new EM candidates, but changes each
bank's ranking and can change the bootstrap and original winners differently.
This is why stability must be recomputed rather than copied from the old score.

## Measure only the requested cells

```{r policies}
targeted <- CECrescoreGrid(g,rsi_policy="nontrivial_unsaturated")
targeted$summary[,c("C","lambda","REO","sat","measured","rsi","keep")]
```

For fixed grids, policies apply to the final representative. Adaptive component
traversal applies them to candidate test points in the frozen pilot. The table
describes eligibility; testing can stop before every eligible point is visited:

| Policy | Requirement for measurement |
|:--|:--|
| `all` | All cells, including trivial and saturated cells |
| `unsaturated` | `sat == 0` |
| `nontrivial_unsaturated` | `sat == 0` and `REO > 1` |
| `saturation_band` | `sat <= rsi_saturation_max` |

The band defaults to 0.10 in a fitting call. Its value is preserved by
`CECrescoreGrid`; changing that band limit requires a fitting call with the
desired limit, optionally reusing its complete checkpoint. The final retention
threshold is separate. For example, measure in the band `sat <= 0.10`, then
retain only `sat <= 0`.

If L < 2 or B = 0, the required diagnostic is missing. A missing value is not
replaced by one and does not satisfy the filter. To restore measurement on
an excluded trivial cell, use `all` or `unsaturated` rather than assigning a
stability value by convention.

Adaptive CEM defaults to the saturation band. Its pilot calibrates and refines
without any L+B campaigns; only eligible active cells then receive the repeated
fits. Pilot children receive parent starts, while independent campaigns do not.
With `diagnostic_strategy="cells"`, better measurement results can improve the
diagram and reactivate boundaries; check `$adaptive$final_refinement_pending`.
The default component strategy keeps the pilot fixed. EM banks are fitted once
across the grid, so their measurement policy skips comparisons, not EM generation.

## Regional measurement and reference bootstrap

Adaptive diagrams default to `diagnostic_strategy="components"` in
`adaptive_control`. The calibrated pilot is frozen; edge-connected cells with
the same partition form a component. Eligible test points are ordered by
distance to its area-weighted barycentre in raw `(log C, lambda)` coordinates.
Testing stops at the first strict diagnostic success. The final saturation
mask remains separate from the policy limiting which points are tested.

`measured` identifies direct campaigns. Regional values carry
`diagnostic_origin="component_witness"` and their source cell in
`diagnostic_witness`; `_direct` columns retain the actual pointwise values.
`adaptive$components` stores the geometry, ordering and stopping decisions.
Use `adaptive_control=list(diagnostic_strategy="cells")` for pointwise coverage.

At every measured point, the best original execution is compared with the
grid representative, before filtering. Independent Stab_algo and independent RSI
must both be strictly above their respective requested thresholds. The best original must disagree with the
representative below that threshold, and it must not improve its score. Only
then is the representative fixed. Each existing bootstrap receives one CEM descent from its indexed
labels. Stab_algo is then one by construction, and RSI is the mean agreement
of frozen bootstrap projections with that reference. Raw independent values
remain in the `_raw` columns and the complete records in `measurements`.
Either independent diagnostic at or below its threshold leaves these diagnostics
unchanged and cannot trigger a conditional bootstrap. In particular, a poor
independent RSI cannot be rescued by this rule.
`reference_bootstrap=FALSE` restores independent-only diagnostics.

## Use the same bootstrap samples across analyses

```{r shared-bootstrap}
set.seed(19)
indices <- replicate(3,sample.int(nrow(X),nrow(X),replace=TRUE),simplify=FALSE)
paired <- CECfitBoundGrid(Z=X,C_grid=1,lambda_grid=1,
  optimization="em_bank",penalty="none",k0=3,B=3,
  bootstrap_indices=indices,algo_seed=20,
  optimizer_control=list(Rmax=3,Ninit=1,max_iter=20))
stopifnot(identical(paired$bootstrap_indices,indices))
```

This controls resampling in addition to optimizer seeds. Bootstrap outputs
are selected on their own training samples and projected using frozen learned
parameters. They are evaluated for agreement on the original rows, not on
the resampled row sequence with duplicates.

The exposed `CECstability()` function can evaluate another clustering method
once that method's independent outputs have been expressed as labels on those
same reference observations. It does not itself fit or project another method.

## Reuse a complete fitting checkpoint

```{r checkpoint}
cache <- tempfile("cec-cache-")  # use a persistent project path for real work
args <- list(Z=X,C_grid=1,lambda_grid=c(0.8,1.2),
  optimization="em_bank",penalty="none",k0=2,B=2,algo_seed=23,
  optimizer_control=list(Rmax=2,Ninit=1,max_iter=15),
  checkpoint_dir=cache,resume=TRUE,n_cores=1)
first <- do.call(CECfitBoundGrid,args)
again <- do.call(CECfitBoundGrid,args)
stopifnot(identical(first$banks,again$banks),
          identical(first$summary,again$summary))
```

For fixed grids and EM banks, each completed repetition is checkpointed,
and EM additionally records each
completed start and its random-generator state. A matching partial cache can
resume interrupted fitting. A complete cache skips fitting but still evaluates
scores and diagnostics. Changed seeds, data or budgets
invalidate it. `force_recompute=TRUE` explicitly ignores it.

Adaptive CEM separately checkpoints each pilot fit, each execution within a
cell's independent campaign, and each completed harmonization. On resume,
mesh decisions are replayed from these saved numerical outputs. Its
`$executions` table identifies the reused records; `$measurements` preserves
independent outputs, projections and diagnostics by cell ID.

EM cache identity is independent of penalty and grid because these only rank
the candidates, provided the stored Cmax covers every target. CEM cache identity
includes the cells and penalty because CEM searches optimize those objectives.

Automatic result names are based on fitting identity. Several EM scoring grids
can therefore share an automatic name. Use explicit distinct `saveRDS` paths
when preserving paired analyses. Results include the original data, so ordinary
data-sharing restrictions still apply to the saved object.

## Parallelism and full elapsed time

```{r parallel, eval=FALSE}
timed <- system.time(g_parallel <- CECfitBoundGrid(Z=X,
  C_grid=c(0.25,1),lambda_grid=c(0.6,1,1.5),
  optimization="em_bank",penalty="none",k0=20,B=20,algo_seed=17,
  optimizer_control=list(Rmax=10,Ninit=5,Cmax=2),n_cores=4))
timed[["elapsed"]]
```

Workers handle independent repetitions. Fixed master seeds give the same
randomization regardless of scheduling. A direct new-engine `CECclassif`
call uses one core; use the grid interface to parallelize repetitions.
`meta$fitting_elapsed` is only the fitting stage, so it is not the total
time of the pipeline. Record outer elapsed time, budgets, cores and data
dimensions for comparisons. A faster run is not evidence of equal search quality.

## Common situations

| Observation | What to inspect |
|:--|:--|
| No retained cells | Measurement policy, L and B, saturation and the two separate stability thresholds |
| Only one group | Candidate counts, failed starts, budget stops, C and lambda; one group may also be a valid outcome |
| Same REO at several cells | Compare labels or `partition_id`, not group count alone |
| RSI above one | The ratio is not clipped; inspect both averages |
| Unexpected plot selection | Supply C and lambda explicitly; omitted coordinates use a display default |
| A saved fit seems to have ignored changes | Check engine, controls, seeds and version in `meta`; old script arguments may be compatibility-only |
| Source installation fails | Check the R version, C++ toolchain and `RcppArmadillo`; the supplied Windows binary avoids local compilation |

The maintained reference is available through `?CECoptimizers`,
`?CECdiagnostics`, `?CECresults`, and the function-specific help pages.
